builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Nudging Decision Models: Do Digital Nudges Steer Fast, Generation-Free AI Agents?
summary: Replaces text-generating LLM agents for option-selection steps with non-generative decision models that output a choice directly, cutting inference latency and API cost. Costs include adopting a distinct model class (Jev, Decision-1, d1) that may not be accessible via standard APIs, plus added behavioral fragility. Can fail by being steered unintentionally: defaults and social-influence signals dominate choices in a System 1 pattern, risking compliance, fairness, and robustness problems in production.
rationale: The speed and cost benefit is plausible for constrained infrastructure, but the demonstrated extreme susceptibility to nudges and the unavailability of the evaluated models make production adoption premature without workload-specific validation.
technique: Generation-free decision models for agent choices

claims.statement: Replaces text-generating LLM agents for option-selection steps with non-generative decision models that output a choice directly, cutting inference latency and API cost. Costs include adopting a distinct model class (Jev, Decision-1, d1) that may not be accessible via standard APIs, plus added behavioral fragility. Can fail by being steered unintentionally: defaults and social-influence signals dominate choices in a System 1 pattern, risking compliance, fairness, and robustness problems in production.

The abstract asserts decision models are far faster and less costly than LLM agents, but provides no factor; reported metrics are behavioral (97.5-99.9% default uptake, 75-96% social-influence uptake vs 47-49% control).
